diagnosis: The optimization is stuck because the mutations are adding complexity and length to an already dense skill, leading to cognitive overload for the model. The initial drop from a perfect 36/36 score was likely caused by the introduction of a placeholder `{{...}}` which, combined with the multi-account logic, created a new failure path. Subsequent mutations, while logically sound, added more prose, rules, and examples (`Account Selection`, `--forward` example, placeholder handling logic). This has increased the difficulty for the model to extract the core command syntax from the surrounding explanatory text. The skill has become a detailed user manual when what the model needs is a quick and unambiguous API reference. The current approach of adding more clarifying text is having the opposite effect and is entrenching the local optimum.

The skill is stuck in a local optimum of "brittle perfection." It has reached a maximum effective information density for the model, where its high performance is fragile. The successful Round 5 mutation (restructuring for clarity) indicates the model heavily relies on scannable structure over prose. Subsequent mutations, even minor ones like tweaking placeholders (Rounds 8 & 9), have degraded performance by introducing subtle inconsistencies or removing previously learned structural cues. The optimization loop is failing because it continues to apply incremental, additive changes to a system that is already at its cognitive load limit. The core problem is no longer missing information, but rather the cognitive overhead of parsing the existing, dense information.
